lineage.strategy: Move from syndicated earnings evidence to the SEC 10-Q for backlog composition, conversion timing, liquidity and explicit data-center concentration risks.

observations.fact: Powell reported $2.4 billion backlog at June 30, 2026, with about $1.3 billion expected to be recognized within 12 months; commercial/other industrial represented 40% of backlog and oil/gas excluding petrochemical and electric utility each represented 24%.

The filing states roughly $800 million of data-center infrastructure projects were awarded in the first nine months of fiscal 2026, including one order above $400 million and two additional orders above $75 million each.
Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments were $633.6 million at June 30, while nine-month operating cash flow was $195.0 million.

risks.risk: Powell explicitly warns backlog can be cancelled or modified and that increasing data-center exposure may change product mix and add demand/regulatory concentration risks.

unknowns.unknown: The filing does not disclose customer identity or project-level margin for the largest data-center awards, limiting concentration and profitability attribution.

recommendation: Use SEC backlog composition, near-term conversion and liquidity as source-addressed underwriting inputs; separately stress cancellation, customer concentration and data-center mix effects.
